chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub al-Zarrad, from Abu Ayyub, from Abu al-Ward, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) addressed the people on the last Friday of Sha'ban, so he praised God and extolled Him,
then he said: 'O people, a month has overshadowed you in which is a night
God made its fasting obligatory and made the standing in prayer of one night within it, by voluntary prayer, like one who voluntarily prays for seventy nights in the other months.

And He made for one who voluntarily performs in it a characteristic from the characteristics of goodness and piety, like the reward of one who fulfills an obligation from the obligations of God, Exalted and Glorified.
And whoever fulfills in it an obligation from the obligations of God, Exalted and Glorified, is like one who fulfills seventy obligations from the obligations of God in the other months.
And it is the month of patience, and indeed patience's reward is Paradise, and it is the month of sharing.
And it is a month in which God increases the provision of the believers.
And whoever breaks the fast of a fasting believer in it, for him with God is thereby the freeing of a neck and forgiveness of his sins for what has passed.
It was said to him: O Messenger of God, not all of us can afford to break the fast of a fasting person.

So he said: 'Indeed God, the Exalted, is Generous; He gives this reward to one who can afford nothing but a sip of milk with which he breaks the fast from that, or a drink of fresh water, or a date, who cannot afford more than that.
And whoever eases for his slave in it, God will ease his reckoning.
And it is a month whose beginning is mercy, its middle is forgiveness, and its end is acceptance and freeing from the Fire.
And you have no need in it to be without four characteristics: two characteristics by which you please God, and two characteristics by which you have no need to be without them.
As for the two by which you please God, they are the testimony that there is no god but God and that I am the Messenger of God.
And as for the two by which you have no need to be without them, you ask God in it for your needs and Paradise, and you ask for well-being and seek refuge in Him from the Fire.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards and virtues of the month of Ramadan according to the Prophet's sermon in Sha'ban?
ai.summary: This sermon, known as the 'Sermon of the Last Friday of Sha'ban,' serves as a pivotal prophetic address in Shia tradition, marking the transition from Sha'ban to Ramadan with specific spiritual directives. It underscores the concept of 'Muwasah' (generosity in sustenance) and highlights the unique temporal structure of the month, where the first third is mercy, the middle is forgiveness, and the last is deliverance from Hellfire. The hadith also provides practical flexibility for those with limited means, emphasizing that even a sip of water or a date suffices for the reward of freeing a slave.
